title: R_3(5(x-y)=3z) = 125
statement: The 3-colour Rado number of the equation 5(x-y) = 3z is exactly 125: every 3-colouring of {1,...,125} contains a monochromatic solution, and some 3-colouring of {1,...,124} avoids one.

concept_refs.note: authored this session at math-education graph/concepts/rado-number.md (uncommitted); flip to resolved with a fresh graph_pin once that repo commits
Rado numbers are the arithmetic-Ramsey analogue: the same threshold/colouring reasoning at a different structure

evidence.notes: RE-CERTIFIED 2026-08-12 inside axeyum's own stack: the proof was produced by the in-tree proof-producing CDCL core streaming TEXT DRAT to disk (0.003 s, 337 steps), read back through axeyum's own parse_drat, and re-derived by axeyum's own backward DRAT checker (0.004 s). No external solver and no external checker took part. SUPERSEDES the original kissat certificate (sha256 5d87485021768a4c7dba5c70560e9c0cd480204e7d24ded2d050d278a0cfd575, 17506 bytes), which was BINARY DRAT: drat-trim verified it, but axeyum's own parse_drat reads text DRAT, so the shipped system could not read the certificate it shipped (findings register B8). The deciding CNF beside it regenerates byte-identically from the claim's parameters.
